findings.title: TECH-SPEC's 'bound the whole handler incl. batch' timeout model contradicts the v1 fix that gave each parallel batch command its own full timeout
findings.claim: TECH-SPEC.md:437 says ctx_execute's fixed timeout 'bounds the whole handler incl. batch'. This is a shared-budget model: one timeout clock for a whole ctx_batch_execute call, which issue #947 ('batch timeout does not bound indexing/search') already pushed the spec toward. But v1 explicitly reversed a shared-budget design for batch concurrency: commit 4fe9c33d ('feat(batch_execute): opt-in concurrency for parallel command runs') states as its own design point 'gives each command its own full timeout instead of shared budget', and ships tests/bench/batch-execute-parallel.ts showing 3.39x speedup at concurrency=8 that depends on each worker getting its own clock, not a shared one divided across workers.
findings.evidence: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY 4fe9c33d4543df0c32172698297bf349f721a99, 'feat(batch_execute): opt-in concurrency for parallel command runs', v1 cm-main. ORIGINAL_INTENT (quoted commit message): 'Add concurrency field (default 1, max 8) to ctx_batch_execute. Serial path preserved bit-for-bit at concurrency=1. Parallel path uses inline worker pool (no new deps), preserves output order via index-keyed array, gives each command its own full timeout instead of shared budget.' REGRESSION_RISK: if v2's GP4/§6.437 timeout model is read literally ('bounds the whole handler incl. batch'), a batch of N parallel commands each needing close to the per-call timeout would starve each other under one shared clock, undoing the exact fix 4fe9c33d made and regressing #947's sibling tickets (#961 byte budget for batch, #1177 batch + compound shell commands) which all assume per-command execution semantics survive in batch mode. TECH-SPEC.md's GP4 row (line 292) only lists `ctx_execute`, not `ctx_batch_execute`, as the tested surface for 'timeoutMs' — there is no GP row anywhere (grep of all '| GP' rows in TECH-SPEC.md) that names `ctx_batch_execute` as the system under test, even though 6 issues in tickets/map-I2.md, map-I3.md and v2-issue-map.md (#1077, #1068, #1048, #1003, #961, #954, #951, #947, #925, #1177) explicitly write their Given/When/Then against `ctx_batch_execute`, not `ctx_execute`.
findings.fix: SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the per-command timeout model from 4fe9c33d for parallel batch workers (do not re-introduce a shared handler-wide clock across concurrent commands); reserve 'bounds the whole handler' language for the serial/concurrency=1 path only, or restate it as 'bounds each command's own execution, and the batch call as a whole is bounded by max(per-command timeouts) under the concurrency setting, not a shared budget'. Add a GP4b (or extend GP4) row naming `ctx_batch_execute` explicitly as a tested tool, with the #947/#961/#1177/#925/#951/#1068 Given/When/Then cases from tickets/map-I2.md and map-I3.md as its golden cases, including a concurrency>1 case asserting per-command timeouts are independent.

findings.title: GS6's two coexisting budget framings (40ms wall vs 20ms-CPU-above-bare-Node) are internally restated three times across TECH-SPEC and ADR-0008 without a single resolved number, and this round's prior reviews (BOTTLENECKS-r4 #5/#6, REVIEW-r4a #31) already flag the arithmetic contradiction but not the fact that it is also unresolved in ADR-0008 itself
findings.claim: BOTTLENECKS-r4.md items 5 and 6, and REVIEW-r4a.md item 31, correctly flag that GS6 states two different units (40ms wall for Claude Code vs 20ms CPU above a 45.6ms bare-Node baseline for command-hook agents) with no single combined pass/fail number, and that the fallback implied ('mcp_tool starts no process' vs try-Bun-else-Node for others) may itself be a disallowed fallback chain. Checking the actual ADR that owns this decision (ADR-0008) shows the same unresolved state was already present at the ADR-authoring stage, not introduced later by TECH-SPEC: ADR-0008 line 72 states the identical 45.6ms-vs-40ms contradiction as an open 'Proposal', not a decision, and DECISIONS-r3.md (searched for a Q4/Q5/GS6 entry) has no entry closing it out. The owner's decision log does not show GS6 was ever ratified with one number.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md:72 ('Proposal: "≤ 20 ms CPU on top of bare Node" for the command-hook agents; Claude Code uses `mcp_tool` and starts no process.') is still phrased as a proposal, and grep over docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md for GS6/Q4/Q5/hook-budget terms returned no match, confirming the owner never closed this specific sub-decision even though DECISIONS-r3 is titled as covering Q1-Q19.
findings.fix: Route this to the owner as an explicit open question (it is not yet answered by DECISIONS-r3 Q1-Q19 despite being load-bearing for GS6/GP3 pass criteria): ask for one ratified end-to-end wall-clock number per agent class, and update ADR-0008:72 from 'Proposal' to a dated decision once answered, so the next round's lint/decisions pass can treat GS6 as settled instead of re-finding it as open every round.
